learningObjectives: State the requested outcome, exact file paths or scope boundary, and the fixed schema or acceptance check that defines 'done' before dispatching any agent.
State the permitted operation explicitly — read-only investigation, a proposed patch for review, or an authorized edit — since an agent not told it may only investigate will sometimes edit anyway.
Require exact commands and verbatim counts (test counts, line counts, exit codes) in every returned report, and recognize a rounded-up summary as a report to send back.
Decide whether a dispatch is even warranted: only when a distinct finding, implementation, or verification result can actually change the next decision.
definitions: Brief: the complete instruction set handed to a subagent that has no memory of the dispatching conversation — a subagent is born knowing only what the brief states.
Verbatim evidence: an exact command and its exact output (a test count, an exit code), never a summary that rounds a partial result up to a full one.
One agent, one scope: a dispatched agent's file territory is disjoint from every other agent working concurrently on the same tree.
Permitted operation: the explicit statement of what the agent may do to the target — read-only investigation, proposed patch, or authorized edit — distinct from what it is being asked to find out.
facilitationPlan: Live 90-minute session. Open with a real, dated failure case: a dispatched agent classified its own org's published work as 'unrelated' third-party content because its brief never stated who owned what it was looking at — the fix that followed was a standing rule that every brief states ownership ground truth. Walk 'Write a complete brief or don't dispatch' from the agent-dispatch-discipline-plugin's SKILL.md line by line: outcome, exact paths, permitted operation, and the fixed 'done' check. Each participant brings one real backlog item from their own repository; in breakout pairs, they draft a complete brief for it live within 20 minutes, then trade with a partner whose only job is to find what a subagent with zero context would misunderstand or invent. Reconvene and have each participant name, out loud, the exact 'done' measure they wrote and the one operation-permission sentence they added.
humanFrame: A brief is not a request to a colleague who shares your context — it is a complete world-state handoff to an amnesiac. Treat every ambiguity left out of the brief as a decision you are silently delegating to the agent's guesswork, and decide on purpose whether that delegation is safe.
assessment: Given an incomplete brief (a one-sentence task description with no scope, no permitted-operation statement, and no acceptance check), participants identify at least three missing elements the brief-writing checklist requires and rewrite it as a dispatch-ready brief within 15 minutes.
